The RENDERING MEDIUM (raster vs vector) brings crispness, interactivity and shared road vertices. A vector city placed through the same cityBox misaligns exactly as the raster does.

principle: Every reference that stays anchored on zoom does so because its detail is authored in, or registered upstream into, one frame: swisstopo's LV95 tile grid (every WMTS layer, the 1864 sheets included, builds its grid from the same projection and only the Time dimension changes), the 3D Tiles transform chain (each tile's transform maps to its parent's frame; Tokyo uses one metric frame), or OSM-derived vector tiles whose decoder already knows the frame. None stays anchored because it is vector: swisstopo enables its vector base only where the renderer supports the frame, and Leaflet's L.svgOverlay extends L.ImageOverlay. The atlas has the frame (CRS.Simple atlas px, NZ=4; the era pyramids already share it), but cityBox(a,w,h) does not register city art into it: it centres a FOOT_R[kind] box (capital 26, town 14, village 9, ruin 8 world px) on the anchor and reads nothing the art depicts. So the vectorised city the owner proposes must be built in, or registered into, atlas coordinates (control points on coast, river mouths, road exits and the ring-dot, one stored transform used by the overlay, the POIs and any vector geometry), not placed through cityBox; built that way, it then adds crispness past cityMaxZ, hover/tap interactivity and shared road vertices.

rows.mechanism: Every WMTS layer, the time series included, builds its WMTSTileGrid from the projection's resolution steps, tile origin and extent (truncated per layer at its maxResolution), on an LV95 View with fixed resolutions. Changing the year only calls updateDimensions({Time}) on the same source; the client never re-fits or re-places a sheet. That the old sheets are georeferenced upstream into LV95 with control points is inference plus search summaries (swisstopo pages blocked).
rows.tag: [registration] (one frame = shared tile grid, not a shared medium)

reverified.outcome: confirmed with wording fix (VL1, C5); not re-verifiable (VL3, C6)
reverified.note: Re-fetched 2026-10-07. OpenLayersWMTSLayer.vue: "return new WMTSTileGrid({ resolutions: resolutionSteps.map((step) => step.resolution), origin: projection.value.getTileOrigin(), ... extent: projection.value.bounds.flatten" and "layer.getSource().updateDimensions(wmtsTimeConfig.value.dimensions)"; createTileGridForProjection slices resolutionSteps at indexOfMaxResolution, so it is "same grid, truncated per layer", not "same grid at every zoom" (dissent upheld on wording). useViewBasedOnProjection: "resolutions: constants.LV95_RESOLUTIONS, projection: LV95.epsg". GeoAdminWMTSLayer.class.js checks constants.SWISSTOPO_TILEGRID_RESOLUTIONS.includes(maxResolution). CesiumWMTSLayer.vue calls getWmtsXyzUrl(... addTimestamp: true). The upstream georeferencing method, sheet counts, datum-shift fix and the Siegfried 0.7 mm tolerance (VL3, C6) rest on blocked hosts and stay unverified.

rows.reference: Tokyo 3D streamed-city post (best candidate github.com/jeantimex/tokyo "Procedural Tokyo", not confirmed as the post) and the 3D Tiles model it echoes
rows.provenance: Post is owner's paraphrase (docs/research/streamed-streets.md); repo and spec read on raw.githubusercontent.com.
rows.mechanism: Tokyo uses one metric world frame with its origin at the area centre and 256 m tiles. In 3D Tiles each tile's transform maps its local frame to its parent's, and child content lies inside the parent's bounding volume, so refinement swaps happen inside one transform chain. The chain preserves registration that was authored in; it does not create it ("cannot move content" is inference).
rows.tag: [registration] (3D Tiles transform chain into one frame)

reverified.note: Tokyo README: "World frame: metres, x east, y up (Tokyo Peil height), z south; the origin is the area's centre." and "Tiles are 256 m squares meshed in Web Workers." 3D Tiles README.adoc: "The `transform` property is a 4x4 affine transformation matrix, stored in column-major order, that transforms from the tile's local coordinate system to the parent tile's coordinate system" and "the content for child tiles are completely inside the parent's bounding volume". The spec guarantees the chain and containment, not cross-level registration (dissent upheld on wording).

rows.transfers: A city detail level should be a child of the atlas frame (atlas px plus one fitted chart-to-atlas transform), nesting inside the coarser sheet, not a separately fitted picture; cityBox is a parent-relative transform whose scale comes from FOOT_R, not from the art.

rows.mechanism: Overlay corners and base tiles go through the same map.project(); _reset runs on every zoom event and rounds corners via latLngToLayerPoint, so Leaflet itself adds about 1 screen px at most, at rest as well as during animation. Placement input is an axis-aligned LatLngBounds only.
rows.tag: [registration] (Leaflet pins the box; the box is where the error is)

reverified.note: ImageOverlay.js: "zoom: this._reset" and "this._map.latLngToLayerPoint(this._bounds.getNorthWest())"; Map.js: "var projectedPoint = this.project(toLatLng(latlng))._round();". C1's "only during the 250 ms animation" is wrong: rounding also happens at rest (dissent upheld on wording).

rows.transfers: The shift is not Leaflet drift: a fixed error of d atlas px shows as d*2^(z-4) screen px, so the fix belongs in what cityBox(a,w,h) feeds the bounds, not in the zoom animation.

rows.provenance: Leaflet docs at v1.9.4 on raw.githubusercontent.com; npm registry README.
rows.mechanism: A map has one CRS; "think in map units" and derive an image's bounds by measuring known coordinates in the image and extrapolating, after the tutorial shows approximate bounds failing. Rotated places an image by three corner points (rotate and skew).

reverified.note: crs-simple.md: "A Leaflet map has one CRS (and *one* CRS *only*)", "**Think in map units**", "Measuring how many pixels there are between the 0 and 1000 coordinates, and extrapolating, we can have the right coordinate bounds for this image". npm README: "defined by **three** points". npm maintainers field lists ivansanchez only; "by a Leaflet maintainer" is in neither source and is dropped.

rows.transfers: cityBox is the tutorial's "approximate bounds" case: replace it with bounds measured from control points (coast, river mouths, road exits, the ring-dot) fitted to atlas px.

rows.provenance: npm registry READMEs; IIIF georef spec on raw.githubusercontent.com.
rows.mechanism: Ground control points (image px to map coordinates) solve one transform: straight and Helmert need 2 GCPs, polynomial1 3, polynomial2 6, polynomial3 10, thin-plate spline 3 (exact at GCPs), projective 4. The same transform warps rasters (WebGL2, triangle by triangle) and vectors vertex by vertex, with optional midpoint refinement (off by default).
rows.tag: [registration] (one transform applied to raster and vector alike)

reverified.note: @allmaps/transform 1.0.0-beta.53 README table re-read: helmert "Applies translation, scaling and rotation. Preserves shapes and angles. | 2"; thinPlateSpline "Transformation is 'exact' at GPCs. | 3"; "By default, `maxDepth = 0` and no refinement is applied." @allmaps/leaflet 1.0.0-beta.55: "uses WebGL to transform images", "works in browsers and in Node.js as an ESM or an UMD module" (so not ESM-only), and the zoomAnimationThreshold: 1 comment. "EPSG:3857" is not named in either README and is dropped.

rows.transfers: Port the method, not the library: an offline, deterministic chart-px to atlas-px fit (translation plus scale first, Helmert if rotation matters) stored as data, used by the raster overlay, the POIs and any future vector city alike; TPS bends canon art and needs an owner ruling.

rows.provenance: npm registry READMEs; DistortableImage source on raw.githubusercontent.com.
rows.mechanism: Runtime registration without WebGL: three corners (affine) or four corners (perspective, CSS matrix3d). DistortableImage writes only the end-state matrix on zoomanim and lets the CSS transition interpolate, which need not follow the tiles' path.

reverified.note: npm READMEs: "This plugin has been tested only with Leaflet 1.0.0-beta and 1.0.0-rc1."; "allows for perspectival distortions of images, client-side, using CSS3 transformations in the DOM"; "It can handle over 100 images smoothly, even on a smartphone" (self-reported).

rows.transfers: If a fit needs rotation, either pre-warp offline into a plain axis-aligned overlay or use a small in-file corner-placed layer; do not vendor either plugin, and keep the POIs and wash on the same transform.

rows.provenance: raw.githubusercontent.com/mapbox/vector-tile-spec.
rows.mechanism: A vector tile carries no frame of its own: geometry is integers in a tile-local extent and the decoder must already know the tile's bounds and projection.
rows.tag: [registration] (vectors align only because the frame is agreed before encoding)

reverified.note: Quote recorded by both verifiers: "A Vector Tile SHOULD NOT contain information about its bounds and projection."

rows.transfers: A city plan in its own local frame (genCityCanvas's 2048 canvas, a traced DM chart, an MFCG export) needs an explicit local-to-atlas transform before any layer draws it; choosing vector gives no alignment for free.

rows.reference: MapLibre style spec zoom rules; OpenMapTiles / OSM Bright / OSM Carto building ladder
rows.provenance: npm tarball @maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec 26.4.4; raw.githubusercontent.com (openmaptiles, osm-bright-gl-style, maplibre-gl-js, openstreetmap-carto).
rows.mechanism: ["zoom"] may drive only a top-level step or interpolate; layers have minzoom gates; source maxzoom data is reused at deeper zooms. Buildings arrive as merged blocks at z13 (DBSCAN cluster, buffer-union, VW simplify) and individual polygons from z14.

reverified.note: latest.json: "`["zoom"]` may only appear as the input to a top-level `"step"` or `"interpolate"` expression"; minzoom "At zoom levels less than the minzoom, the layer will be hidden."; source maxzoom "Data from tiles at the maxzoom are used when displaying the map at higher zoom levels." building.sql: "<z13> z13 | <z14_> z14+"; update_building.sql: ST_ClusterDBSCAN(... eps := zres14 ...) and ST_SimplifyVW. Wording: step is not continuous, and only OSM Bright's building-top layer has the 13-16 opacity ramp (dissent upheld on wording).

rows.transfers: If a vector city is built, band it (block hulls first, footprints later, thresholds chosen with filigree), but banding is rendering density and does nothing for the anchoring the owner asked about.

reverified.note: StreetView3DOverlay README: "There are a number of parameters related to the Street View Panoramas which have been established by trial-and-error. This means that both the position and orientation of the ferris wheel is not very precise." js-three README: "All computations on the GPU related to the position use float32 numbers, which limits the possible precision to about 7 decimal digits." The anchor is set by setAnchor(), not fixed, and the source says "not very precise", not "drifts" (dissent upheld on wording).

rows.transfers: Do not hand-nudge city bounds until they look right: fit control points and report the residual in atlas px; the float32 point matters only for a future WebGL layer (living H1), since Leaflet overlays use float64.
